articleTitle: Micro-hotplate for thin film gas sensor: fabrication using cmos technology
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper reports a novel approach to fabricate micro hotplate for thin film gas sensor. The approach uses frontside anisotropic etching of silicon together with special layout to create the thermally isolated structure. Sandwich of inter-dielectric layers and aluminum interconnection provides the supporting material while highly doped boron diffusion provides the heating and temperature sensing. The design incorporates guard heater layout that improves the temperature uniformity. Simulation result shows that the temperature variation on a sensor film of 50 x 60 /spl mu/m/sub 2/ is less than 20 /spl deg/C when the operating temperature is 350 /spl deg/C. The micro-hotplate fabricated exhibits heating efficiency of about 7 /spl deg/C/mW and CMOS compatibility.

articleTitle: The application of delta-doping in heterojunction bipolar transistors
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The spl delta/-doping is applied to the EB junction of single heterojunction bipolar transistors(SHBT) and BC junction of double heterojunction bipolar transistors(DHBT). Very good results are obtained. The offset voltage is reduced in SHBT and dramatically current gain increase is obtained in DHBT.

articleTitle: Radiation hardness of fluorinated oxides prepared by liquid phase deposition method following rapid thermal oxidation
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Liquid phase deposition (LPD) following rapid thermal oxidation (RTO) is proposed as a method to obtain the fluorinated gate oxides. The radiation effect on these fluorinated oxides prepared by various sequences is studied. It was experimentally observed that all the fluorinated gate oxides are more radiation hard than the rapid thermal oxide (control oxide). Interestingly, the amount of fluorine (F) incorporated in the gate oxides can be easily and precisely controlled by changing the sequences and the times of LPD process and/or RTO treatment.

articleTitle: The effects of AlGaAs cap layers on the dc and speed performance of GaAs metal-semiconductor-metal photodetectors
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The effects of AlGaAs cap layers for GaAs metal-semiconductor-metal photodetectors (MSM-PD's) have been investigated. By changing the thickness of the AIGaAs cap layer (i.e. 30 nm, 60 nm and 90 nm), both DC and speed performance are analyzed and discussed. Meanwhile, two cap structures with abrupt and graded hetero-junction, respectively, were also grown for comparison. The results of this work show that adding a 30 nm-thick AIGaAs cap layer can greatly suppress the low frequency internal gain and lead to improved linearity. At 5 V bias, the rise time and the full-width at half maximum (FWHM) of such 100 /spl mu/m x 100 /spl mu/m devices are measured to be 28 ps and 39 ps, respectively, corresponding to a bandwidth exceeding 10 GHz. The devices with a thicker cap layer, however, have significant internal gain and lower speed response due to the formation of a thicker barrier blocking the photocarriers to reach the electrodes.

articleTitle: Process and device characterization of a gated-field-emission triodes for flat-panel display application
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Gated-Field-Emission Triode from the cone-tip formation process to its emission properties has been systematically characterized. Process simulation shows that the successful formation of the micro tip structure is mainly determined by the migration length of the e-beam evaporated layer. The measured triode characteristics matches well with the simulated program in the saturation region with proper tip radius adjustment without an artificial enhancement factor. The calculated enhancement factor matches well with other published data.

articleTitle: Heterojunction bipolar transistor technology for analog and digital applications
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper describes high performance AlGaAs/GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) technologies developed at Rockwell and their applications to digital, analog, microwave and multifunction circuits. The GaAs BBT technology is relatively mature and is being transferred to pilot production at Rockwell. The AIGaAs/GaAs HBT technology provides transistors with high fmax (up to 218 GHz), high f/sub t/ (up to 98 GHz), high Early Voltage (V/sub a/ > 200 V), high breakdown voltage (BV/sub cbo = 15-45 V), a wide range of choice of dc current gain (10-200), and MSI LST integration levels. GaAs HBTs have also demonstrated high power-added efficiency for microwave amplification of both discrete transistors (67.8% at 10 GHz) and MMICs (minimum 43% over 7-11 GHz). Moreover, both digital and analog/microwave GaAs HBT circuits have been successfully fabricated on the same wafer. As a result, a monolithic integration of multifunction circuits becomes feasible and will open a new area for direct digital signal processing at microwave frequencies.

articleTitle: Fabrication of gated field emitter arrays for vacuum microtriodes
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Field emitter arrays of very sharp silicon tips have been fabricated using wet chemical etching technique. High depth to-width ratio silicon tips have been also fabricated using the semi-anisotropic dry etching technique. After the oxidation sharpening process, uniformly sharp emitter tips has been achieved. A new self-aligned process to fabricate the gated emitter arrays has been successfully developed. By this method, the tip radius is about 25 nm, and the gate aperture diameters can be easily reduced to 1.2 /spl mu/m and even more. This will largely decrease the turn-on voltage of the field emission devices.

articleTitle: Recent progress in quantum well infrared photodetectors and imaging arrays
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A review of the recent progress in III-V quantum well infrared photodetectors (QWIPs) for focal plane arrays (FPAs) staring infrared imaging system applications is presented in this paper. A discussion of the device physics of the intersubband absorption and hot-carrier transport processes for different types of bound-to-continuum (BTC) and bound-to-miniband (BTM) transition QWIPs is given. The performance parameters such as dark current, spectral responsivity, and detectivity of III-V QWIPs having different structures and materials are discussed. Design of the grating couplers for efficient coupling of normal incidence IR radiation into the quantum wells of n-type QWIPs will be addressed. In addition, a new class of normal incidence p-type strained-layer III-V QWIPs with high BLIP temperature will be depicted. Finally, a discussion of the high sensitivity large area (128x 128) focal plane arrays using GaAs QWIPs for the staring infrared imaging system will also be given.

articleTitle: Two issues for packaging a high-speed DFB laser array: electrical crosstalk and optical coupling
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We characterized the electrical crosstalk and the optical coupling for a high-speed DFB laser array.

articleTitle: Reactive ion etching of 2 /spl mu/m by 8 /spl mu/m Si deep trench using photoresist as the etching mask
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Anisotropic etching of deep trench in bulk Si for isolating global buried collector in Si monolithic microwave integrated circuit has been successfully developed with SF/sub 6//C/sub 2/CIF/sub 3/ gas mixtures. Using photoresist as the etching mask, deposition of polymer thin film on the sidewalls of the trench occurred, hence inhibited lateral etching and made the process anisotropic. Under optimal process conditions, an etching anisotropy of 0.98 and an etching selectivity of silicon to photoresist higher than 28 were observed.

articleTitle: Planarization of deep trench with LOCOS for silicon monolithic microwave integrated circuit
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The self-planarization of deep trench with 2 micron thick field oxidation has been developed for Si monolithic microwave integrated circuit (Si MMIC). Trenches with geometry of 2 /spl mu/m wide by 6/spl mu/m deep can be filled and planarized simply by a local oxidation of silicon (LOCOS) without polysilicon re-filling or etching back, while maintained a collector-to-collector leakage of 5 /spl mu/a at 15 V.

articleTitle: Low threshold 1.55 /spl mu/m compressive-strained multiple quantum well lasers for high temperature and high power operation
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We report the fabrication and high temperature operation characteristics of the 1.55 /spl mu/m InGaAsP/InP compressive-strained multiple-quantum-well capped-mesa buried-heterostructure (MQW-CMBH) lasers. The laser performances of low threshold current achieved by compressive-strained multiple quantum wells and effective current blocking obtained by p-n-p-n InP layers are investigated. For as-cleaved lasers, continuous wave (CW) output power more than 6 mW at 100/spl deg/C and pulsed output power up to 51 mW at 20/spl deg/C are demonstrated. The fabricated LDs have been evaluated by reliability testing, and were estimated having lifetime of around 136,000 hours.

articleTitle: High quality thin oxide films formed by using ultra low temperature liquid phase deposition
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We found that an LPD oxide could be deposited on Si substrates even at ultra low temperature while the H/sub 2/O quantity was sufficient to make the solution supersaturated. The dependence of deposition rate on H/sub 2/O quantity and deposition temperature were investigated. By using this ultra low temperature deposition method, a high quality thin LPD film was developed. The LPD oxide with 300 A thick exhibited a very low leakage current of 2 nA/cm/sup 2/ at 4 MV/cm and a high breakdown field over 9 MV/cm.

articleTitle: 1.55 /spl mu/m absorptive-grating complex-coupled distributed feedback lasers with high single-longitudinal-mode yield
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: 1.55 /spl mu/m InGaAsP/InP complex-coupled distri buted feedback lasers with p-InGaAs absorptive grating were demonstrated. With coupling strength of 1.77, single mode yield more than 70 % and side mode suppression ratio as high as 43 dB above two times threshold current were achieved. It has been verified that the presence of gain-coupling strength can eliminate the mode degeneracy effectively.

articleTitle: An analytical a-Si:H TFT DC/ capacitance model using an effective temperature approach for deriving a switching time model
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper presents an analytical a-Si:H DC capacitance model using an effective temperature approach for deriving a switching time model for an inverter circuit considering deep and tail states. Based on the analytical model, the threshold voltage of an a-Si:H TFT is proportional to the deep state density and the switching time of the TFT inverter is dependent on the tail state density.

articleTitle: High peak-to-valley current ratio In/sub 0.3/Ga/sub 0.7/As/In/sub 0.29/Al/sub 0.71/As resonant tunneling diodes grown on GaAs
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We have investigated the current voltage characteristics of In/sub 0.3/Ga/sub 0.7/As/In0.29/Al/sub 0.71/As double-barrier resonant tunneling diodes grown on GaAs substrates. These devices exhibit peak-to-valley current ratios as high as 7.6 and 19.5 at room temperature and 77 K, respectively. Two negative differential resistance regions are also observed for devices with larger well width. These results have shown that high quality epilayer can be obtained despite the large lattice mismatch between In/sub 0.3/Ga/sub 0.7/As and GaAs.

articleTitle: Recent developments in N/sub 2/O- and NO-based oxynitride dielectrics for cmos ulsi applications
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper reviews recent developments in N/sub 2/O- and NO based oxynitride gate dielectrics for CMOS ULSI applications. These dielectrics are extremely attractive due to their process simplicity, thickness controllability, excellent reliability and hot-carrier immunity. In this paper, several issues like growth kinetics, chemical composition, electrical properties and hot-carrier immunity of these dielectrics are discussed. EEPROM applications and thickness scaling issues related to these dielectrics are also discussed.

articleTitle: Silicon-germanium polycrystalline films for TFT applications
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The formation of polycrystalline-Si/sub 1-x/Ge/sub x/ thin films on oxide-coated Si substrates is discussed. Two modes of deposition, thermal growth and plasma-enhanced deposition, were studied using PE-VLPCVD (Plasma-Enhanced Very-Low-Pressure CVD) at /spl les/600/spl deg/C. In both cases, growth rates and grain sizes increase with Ge content, and the polyerystalline-to-amorphous transition temperature is lower for Si/sub1-x/Ge/sub x/ than Si. Compared to thermal growth, plasma-enhanced deposition promotes higher growth rates and improved structural properties such as smoother surface morphology, more columnar [220] oriented grain texture, and direct deposition onto oxide. Post-deposition techniques were explored to enlarge the decreased grain sizes associated with plasma deposition of poly-Si/sub 1-x/Ge/sub x/ compared to thermal growth, without sacrificing other improved properties. Compared to plasma-deposited poly-Si/sub 1-x/Ge/sub x/films, plasma deposition of amorphous-Si/sub1-x/Ge/sub x/ followed by a crystallization anneal at 600/spl deg/C results in films with an even smoother surface and grain sizes enhanced by an order of magnitude. The largest grain sizes, /spl tilde/1.3/spl mu/m, were achieved in poly Si/sub 1-x/Ge/sub x/ films formed by Si+ ion implantation for amorphization with a subsequent recrystallization anneal.

articleTitle: A novel technique to determine the lateral distribution of interface states and oxide-trapped charges in LDD MOSFET's
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Previous studies showed that simultaneous determination of the interface states (N/sub it/) and oxide-trapped charges (Q/sub ox/) in the vicinity of the drain side of MOS devices are rather difficult. A new technique which allows the simultaneous characterization of the spatial distribution of both N/sub it/ and Q/sub ox/, will be presented. Submicron LDD n-MOS devices were tested as a sample and charge pumping measurement are performed. Moreover, the spatial distributions of interface states and oxide trapped charges have been justified by 2-D device simulation results. Results show that simulated drain current characteristics compare well with experimental data.

articleTitle: Design of c+-implantation conditions by TRIM calculation for ion beam defect engineering in Ge/sup +/preamorphized and BF/sub 2/+-implanted silicon
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: TRIM cascade calculations were utilized to simulate the defect production and energy deposition in the ion implanted silicon. A guide line for carbon ion beam defect engineering implant is obtained to reduce the size of residual defects in the high energy Ge+ preamorphized and low energy BF/sub 2/+ implanted silicon.

articleTitle: Composition of selectively grown Ga/sub x/In/sub 1-x/P from high resolution double-crystal x-ray measurement
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The present experiments demonstrate the selective epitaxial growth (SEG) of GalnP by low-pressure metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (LP-MOCVD) using ethyldimethylindium (EDMI), trimethylindium (TMI), trimethylgaflium (TMG) and triethylgallium (TEG) as group III sources. Completely selective epitaxy using TEGa+EDMIn can be achieved at growth temperature of 675/spl deg/C and at growth pressure of 40 Torr, while other combinations (TEG+TNU, TMG+TMI, and TMG+EDMI) can achieve SEG of GaInP at 650/spl deg/C. In epitaxial growth of GaInP, the Ga incorporation efficiency using TEG+EDMI is found to be lower than those using other combinations.

articleTitle: Energy band structure tailoring of InGaAsP/InGaAsP quantum well prepared by organometallic vapor phase epitaxy and measured by photoluminescence
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We report the theoretical and experimental results of the In/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As/sub y/P/sub 1-y//In/sub z/Ga/sub 1-z/As quantum wells (QW). Wafers prepared by low-pressure organometallic vapor phase epitaxy (OMVPE) were studied. The band offset ratios at the heterointerface and material's energy bandgap are determined from the model-solid theory of Van de Walle, while single partical model is used to solve the Schrodinger equation to predict the corresponding wavelength. For unstrained In/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As/sub y/P/sub 1-y//In/sub 0.53/Ga/sub 0.47/As quantum wells, the conduction band offset of bandgap difference (dEc%) can be formulated as: (dEc %)unstrained = 42.6 % - (25.4y) %; on the other hand, for strained In/sub x/Ga/sub 1-x/As/sub y/P/sub 1-y//In/sub z/Ga/sub 1-z/As quantum wells, the strain (S) changes the dEc% as: (dEc%)strain=(dEc%)unstrained + 1.3xS. Results of our samples, measured by photoluminescence and transmission electron microscopy measurements, demonstrate good agreements in devised unstrained QW structure with theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: Factors influencing the oxidation of silicon catalyzed by Cu/sub 3/Si at room temperature
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The dependence of room temperature oxidation of silicon catalyzed by Cu/sub 3/Si on silicide thickness, silicide grain size and the substrate orientation has been investigated by transmission electron microscopy and x-ray diffractometry. articleTitle: Effects of conduction band discontinuity and two dimensional electron gas on the dc characteristics of InAlAs/InGaAs and InAlAs/InAlGaAs DHBT's
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this study, two sets of double heterojunction bipolar transistors (DHBT's) with In/sub 0.52/Al/sub x/Ga/sub 0.48--x/As collector and In/sub 0.53/Al/sub y/Ga/sub 0.47-y/As base were investigated, respectively. It is found that when the conduction band discontinuity of base collector junction is larger than 0.4 eV, an extra two dimensional electron gas (2DEG) will accumulate in the heterojunction notch and enhance the reach-through effect appearing in the output characteristics of DHBT's. This 2DEG effect is strongly dependent on the conduction band discontinuity. After comparing the characteristics of these two sets of DHBT's, we find that hot electron and high collector doping are two approaches which can be used to reduce the 2DEG effect.

articleTitle: Deep center defects in AlGaAs/GaAs GRIN-SCH-SQW lasers fabricated by MBE and MOCVD
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The deep center traps of AlGaAs/GaAs GRIN-SCH SQW lasers fabricated by MBE and MOCVD have been studied using DLTS (Deep Level Transient Spectroscopy) technique.The DLTS spectra show that deep (electron and hole) traps, having larger capture cross sections and concentrations, are observed in n-AlGaAs layers of lasers in addition to the well-known DX center. For the MBE lasers ,deep hole trap H1 may spatially localize in the interfacial regions of discontinous variation Al mole fraction of n AlGaAs layers with X/sub AI/=0.20 /spl rarr/0.43 and X/sub AI/=0.43,and deep electron trap E3 may spatially localize in interfacial regions of discontinous variation Al mole fraction of n AlGaAs layer with X/sub AI/=0.43. For the MOCVD lasers,deep electron trap E3 may spatially localize in n-AlGaAs layers with X/sub Al/0.18 /spl rarr/0.30 and X/sub Al/=0.30 and DX center may spatially localize in the interfacial regions of discontinous variation Al mole fraction of n-AlGaAs layers with X/sub AI/=0.18 /spl rarr/0.30 and X/sub AI/=0.30.

articleTitle: Change of 1/f noise in MOSFETS due to degradation
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Hot-carrier stress in n-channel MOSFETs was investigated. A negative shift in the threshold voltage and a decrease in the drain current were observed. In addition, the degradation increases the series resistance on the drain side. In most cases, the relative 1/f noise in the drain current also increases. The change in the dc characteristics and the 1/f noise indicates that the damage is localised on the drain side for a long-channel device, while it extends along the channel towards the source for a short-channel device. A degraded device is often found to be noisier in its reverse mode than in its normal mode.

articleTitle: The impact of ion-implantation damage on dopant diffusion
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The dopant diffusion has been investigated for silicon substrates implanted with high dosages above the amorphization threshold. Both the transient enhanced diffusion and the uphill diffusion are shown in boron, phosphorus, and arsenic profiles with Si ion implants. The uphill diffusion toward residual damages has been simulated with a phenomenological segregation model. The boron enhanced diffusion with As and P implantation is also affected by the n-type doping besides implant damages.

articleTitle: Electrical properties of barium titanate ferroelectric thin films fabricated by rf magnetron sputtering for memory devices application
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Barium titanate ( BaTiO/sub 3/ ) has recently been studied as a possible dielectric layer for dynamic random access memory (DRAM) and non-volatile memory devices. The BaTiO/sub 3/ ferroelectric thin films are deposited by rf magnetron sputtering. The deposited BaTiO/sub 3/ thin films are annealed at 700 /spl deg/C or 800 /spl deg/C for 1 min in pure O/sub 2/ ambient. The dielectric constant of BaTiO/sub 3/ is measured by using Au/BaTiO/sub 3//Pt/Ti/Si capacitors and is found to be about 120 at an applied frequency of 10 KHz. At an applied electric field of 85 KV/cm, the leakage current density is around 1.5x 10/sup -7/A/cm/sup 2/ for a film thickness 390 nm. The dominant leakage current conduction mechanism is found to be Schottky emission at low applied electric (E<45 KV/cm) and Frenkel-Poole emission at high electric field (E>45KV/cm).

articleTitle: A new process for liquid phase deposition of silicon oxide and its application in amorphous silicon thin film transisitor
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A new process for liquid phase deposition (LPD) of silicon oxide is developed successfully. Both drawbacks in the conventational LPD process: long solution preparation time and low deposition rate, are greatly improved in the present process. This improved LPD process is applied to planarize metal gate of inverted staggered amorphous silicon thin film transistor (TFT). It is found that the device performance is improved by this novel gate planarization process. Besides, the usual leakage problem around the sharp comer of the gate electrode is eliminated.

articleTitle: Itwo x-band monolithic voltage controlled oscillators
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this paper, two types of MMIC voltage controlled oscillators have been successfully demonstrated. The first chip with single tuning diode shows the excellent tuning linearity. The second chip with two tuning diodes can improve the tuning bandwidth. The measured results of VCO with single diode shows the tuning bandwidth of 800 MHz centered at 9.2 GHz with the output power of 12 dBm. The second VCO with dual tuning diodes shows the tuning bandwidth of 2 GHz centered at 9.4 GHz The VCOs are fabricated with Hughes 0.5 micron ion implant MESFET foundry process[1].

publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium

articleTitle: Suppression of boron penetration in BF/sup 2/+ -implanted poly-Si gate using N/sub 2/O oxide and stacked amorphous-silicon (SAS) structure
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Four types of poly-Si gate structure with two types of gate oxide were investigated in this paper to suppress the boron penetration in BF/sup 2/+ -implanted poly Si gate PMOSFET's. Both N/sub 2/O oxide and stacked /spl alpha/-Si structure can effectively suppress the boron penetration.

articleTitle: Effects of the polysilicon etching on the gate oxide damages in an electron cyclotron resonance (ecr) halide-containing plasma
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Effects of the etching of the polysilicon gates on the damages of the thin gate oxides in the electron cyclotron resonance(ECR) plasma have been investigated. The mechnisms for these damages have been estabished. The chlorine containing plasma will directly impinge the oxide and induce a high leakage current. On the other hand, the fluorine-containing plasma can not directly attack the oxide and does not enhance the leakage current.

articleTitle: Effect of plasma treatment of a-SiO/sub x/N/sub y//a-SiN/sub x/ gate insulators on a-Si:H thin-film transistor

articleTitle: A simple adapted gummel method for amorphous silicon device simulation
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The paper present a simple adapted Gummel method (AGM) for amorphous silicon (a-Si) device simulation. The AGM is compared with Gummel method (GM) by two numerical experiments. The comparisons shows the AGM not only converges much faster, but also is more robust than GM. Simulation results show that the AGM is very helpful for a-Si device simulation.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of dynamics of type-II tunneling diodes
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We apply Green's function method, within a two-band model including the coupling between the conduction and light-hole bands, to type-II tunnel diodes with resonant interband tunneling. In contrast to previous models, ours is suitable for studying dynamical responses. The model is applied to the InAs1A1Sb/GaSb/AlSb/InAs structure. In particular, we present results important for device applications, e.g. DC characteristics and AC admittances.

articleTitle: Design, fabrication, and evaluation of a high-performance, low-cost longwave infrared HgCdTe 256x1scanning focal plane array
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium

articleTitle: Lateral field enhanced band-trap-band tunneling current in a 0.5 /spl mu/m "off" state mosfet
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: An interface trap assisted tunneling mechanism which includes hole tunneling from interface traps to the valence band and electron tunneling from interface traps to the conduction band is presented to model the drain leakage current in a 0.5 /spl mu/m LATID n-MOSFET. In the experiment, the device was subject to a DC voltage stress to generate interface traps. Based on our proposed band trap-band tunneling, the increased drain leakage current can be adequately described by an analytical expression of /spl Delta/I/sub d/=Aexp(-B/sub it//F) with a Bit of 13 MV/cm, which is much lower than that (36 MV/cm) of direct band-to-band tunneling.

articleTitle: The study of silicon pressure sensors fabrication
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The objects of this paper focus on the fabrication and characterization of high sensitive silicon pressure sensors. In this experiment, the parameters which may influence the characteristics of sensors including the diaphragm thickness, piezoresistor layout, junction depth and environmental temperature are discussed. articleTitle: Characterization of chemical-mechanical planarization processes
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Chemical mechanical polishing of blanket and patterned oxide films has been studied. Fundamental parameter's governing the planarization technique were examined for the development of the process window as well as for the understanding of the process characteristics. Excellent local and global planarity achieved by chem-mechanical polishing is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Fabrication of multi-channel laser diode array module for parallel optical transmission
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The fabrication of multi-channel laser diode array module for parallel optical transmission was reported. The result showed an average coupling efficiency of 60% from the array module to the fiber optics.

articleTitle: Temperature dependence of porous silicon resistance
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Porous silicon resistors have been fabricated and the resistance at temperatures between 100 K and 400K has been measured in order to investigate the relationship between the temperature dependence of porous silicon resistance and the anodization process. Porous silicon layer was formed in the n/sup +/ region between contacts by anodization in 15 % aqueous HF solution. Anodization time was fixed at 5 minutes and anodization voltage varied. The temperature dependence of the porous silicon resistance varied widely with the anodization voltage. A model explaining the experimental results has been proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Laser ablated pyroelectric thin films for room temperature IR sensors
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: High quality of Sr/sub 0.5/Ba/sub 0.5/Nb/sub 2/O/sub 6/ (SBN50) and Pb/sub 0.95/La/sub 0.05/Ti/sub 0.9875/O/sub 3/ (PLT5) pyroelectric thin films were successfully deposited on Pt-coated silicon by Pulsed Laser Deposition Technique. In this paper, the effect of deposition conditions on the crystallinity and pyroelectricity of SBN50 and PLT thin films was systematically examined. We have found that, SBN50 films have higher dielectric constant /spl epsilon/r of 928 and larger pyroelectric effect (measured by dynamic voltage response) Rv of 1.8*10/sup 3/ V/W at 25 Hz without a poling treatment. Three different PLT films were compared and the PLT5 films possess superior pyroelectric property ( Rv of 1.2*10/sup 3/ V/W at 10 Hz) to the rest two compositions.

articleTitle: A complete drain and substrate current models of oxide damaged submicron LDD MOSFETs
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper describes a Spice-compalible circuit reliability simulation model of submicron LDD MOS devices. It includes an enhanced version of our previous drain current model (Unimos) and a new substrate current model. The substrate current model is developed based on the effective electric field concept which shows a significant improvement to the conventional local field model. The drain current reduction is modeled as mobility degradation due to interface states enhanced scattering. The stressed substrate currmt characteristics are well modeled by considering the variations of the effective electric field. By characterizing the time-dependent of the device parameters, an oxide-damaged I-V model can be obtained. Comparison of the modeled results with those of experimental shows excellent match for a wide range of device channel length, bias conditions and stress time.

articleTitle: The influences of nitrogen, helium, hydrogen, or argon dilution on plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposited a-SiN/sub x/:H
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The effects of dilution gases on hydrogenated amorphous silicon nitride (a-SiN,:H) films were investigated in this study. Silarie and ammonia were used as the reactive species, while nitrogen, helium, hydrogen, and argon were used as the dilution gases in a plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition system at a substrate temperature of 300'C. The total hydrogen concentrations for all a-SiN,:H films were observed to be smaller than 3.OxIO2,2 Cru-3. The dominant mode of electronic conduction would appear to be the Poole Frenkel emission deduced from the current versus voltage (I-V) measurements. The interface trap state density (Dit) which ranged from 3.4xlOII to 1.34012 cm-2eV-1 was evaluated by the C-V characteristics. The influences of dilution gases on a-SiN,:H were also investigated in an application to the performance of the hydrogenated amorphous silicon thin film transistors (a-Si:H TFrs). Analyses of the transfer characteristics of a-Si:H TFrs revealed that the density of deep gap states is 44012 cM-2&V-1 and the field effect mobility p FE) is changing from 0.37 cm'2/V-s to 1.45 cm2/V-s.

articleTitle: Characteristics of amorphous tungsten nitride diffusion barrier for metal-organic chemical vapor deposited Cu metallization
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Copper thin films are deposited on amorphous tungsten nitride diffusion barrier by metal organic chemical vapor deposition method. The resistivity of Cu film is considerably higher than those of Cu films deposited on SiO/sub 2/ boro phospho-silica glass, and Si due to substrate driven reaction. RBS, XTEM and XRD measurements clearly show that 100-800 A amorphous W/sub 67/N/sub 33/, layer successfully executes the role of diffusion barrier for Cu during the annealing process at 800 /spl deg/C for 30 min.

articleTitle: Interface roughness effects on the properties of resonant tunneling hot electron transistor
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The effects of the interface roughness on the resonant tunneling hot electron transistor properties are studied by calculating an average effective transmission coeflicient for the quantum well structure. Our model for the transmission coefficient includes both the quantum interference and the bulk scattering. The interface roughness is represented by a rectangular distribution having the width of one atomic layer. The results indicate that the interface roughness wilI lower and broaden the resonant peak. The emitter peak tunneling current, base current and collector current will be reduced 50% at room temperature. The effect of interface roughness on the gain is relatively weak.

articleTitle: Multislice liquid phase epitaxial, growth of GaP:N yellow-green light-emitting diodes
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A new multislice boat (shown in Fig. 1)system for liquid phase epitaxial(LPE) growth has been developed. This system can successively produce large-scale GaP:N yellow green light-emitting diodes successfully. We use NH/sub 3/ as the nitrogen dopant source of GaP. Because NH/sub 3/ will deplete with increasing distance away from the front. The photocurrent of the individual wafer becomes nonuniformly. However we find successfully that the photo current of four wafers could tend to the same by changing the doping holes density of perforated cover. The averagee value of photocurrent of the uncapsulated 0.5mmx0.5mm die with 5mA forward current can be achieved to 20nA.

articleTitle: Experimental and theoretical investigations of microminiature thermionic vacuum tube devices
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Details on the fabrication and testing of microminiature thermionic vacuum tube devices (i.e., diodes, triodes) with ultra-small (i.e., micron-scale) dimensions will be presented. The micro-miniature thermionic vacuum (MTV) devices can either have a direct or indirect heated cathode with a suspended filament supplying the thermal energy. Single device element architecture can consist of either a totally vertical structure or a combination of planar and vertical structures.

articleTitle: DC and transient analysis of a SiGe-base heterojunction bipolar device with an extended germanium profile into the n- Epi region in an ECL buffer considering high injection
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper reports DC and transient analysis of a SiGe-base HBT with an extended germanium profile into the n-epi region in an ECL buffer. With an extended germanium profile, the unity gain frequency, which suffers less from the high injection degradation, is insensitive to the germanium content. From the pullup transient analysis, with an extended germanium profile. the speed performance of the ECL circuit is less influenced by the high injection effects.

articleTitle: High drain current peak-to-valley ratios in strained In/sub 0.15/Ga/sub 0.85/As channel real-space transfer transistors
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Real-space transfer transistors using a strained ln/sub 0.15/Ga/sub 0.85/As channel layer have been fabricated. The strained InGaAs channel devices show strong negative differential resistance and large drain current peak-to-valley ratio. The peak-to-valley ratio is more than 3000 at room temperature and larger than one million (10/sup 6/) at 77 K. The peak-to-valley ratio is controllable by adjusting the collector voltage.

articleTitle: Nonlinear absorption in n-i-p-i MQWs structure
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The absorption coefficient of the n-i-p-i multi-quantum well(MQW) structure is calculated using an average dipole moment matrix element and variational method. Taking into account both of the excitonic binding energy and shift in absorption subband edge due to the quantum confined Stark effect(QCSE), modulation of the optical absorption spectrum of the structure due to illumination has been analyzed. The calculated absorption peaks arising from le-1hh and le-1lh transitions their changes under optical excitation agree well with the published data. It is found that the exciton peaks' positions are dependent on the bandgap offsets ratio of the quantum well structure. Shifts in the absorption peaks due to illumination is contributed mainly by QCSE, but the contribution due to the change in exciton binding energy is one order of magnitude lower.

articleTitle: In/sub 0.52/Al/sub0.48/As/In/sub 0.53/Ga/sub 0.47/As HEMT's on InP substrates
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In/sub 0.52/Al/sub0.48/As/In/sub 0.53/Ga/sub 0.47/As high electron mobility transistor(HEMT) layer structure were grown by a Riber-32P MBE system on [100] InP:Fe substrates. Devices with 0.8 /spl mu/m gate-length demonstrated a peak extrinsic transconductance of 262 mS/mm at 300 K. A 25% g/sub m/ enhancement was found, once devices were cooled down to 77 K. Microwave characteristics revealed a current gain cutoff frequency(f/sub T/) of 28 GHz and a maximum oscillation frequency (f/sub max/) of 48 GHz at 300 K. Based on the measured S-parameters (45MHz-50GHz), the equivalent circuit model of InO.52AI0.4sAs/ln 0.530ao.47As HEMT's was simulated which will be used for the future monolithic amplifier designs. InO.52AI0.4$AS/InO.53Gao.47As high electron mobility transistor(HEMT) layer structure were grown by a Riber-32P MBE system on [100] InP:Fe substrates. Devices with 0.8,u m gate-length demonstrated a peak extrinsic transconductance of 262 mS/mm at 300 K. A 25% g,,, enhancement was found, once devices were cooled down to 77 K. Microwave characteristics revealed a current gain cutoff frequency(fT) of 28 GHz and a maximum oscillation frequency (f...) of 48 GHz at 300 K.Bsed on the measured S-parameters (45MHz-50GHz), the equivalent circuit model of In/sub 0.52/Al/sub0.48/As/In/sub 0.53/Ga/sub 0.47/As HEMT's was simulated which will be used for the future monolithic amplifier designs.

articleTitle: ONo SMD - a silicon microstrip detector with ONO a-c coupled capacitor
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A single - sided silicon detector with AC-coupling capacitors and Polysilicon bias resistors has been designed and fabricated. The proposed process with ONO (Oxide-Nitride-Oxide) replacing the usual SiO/sub 2/ layer as the dielectric of coupling capacitor in conjunction with a reordering of sequence for layer formation were employed to produce detectors with self-moisture - protection , free from effect of pin-holes and with-high breakdown voltage capacitors. We are performed a series of study to understand the characteristics of the detector. The lowest detector leakage current is about 100nA/cm/sup 2/ at 100 Volts. The breakdown voltage was within 160-200 Volts for the ONO layer, In which we didn' t find any pin - hole out of 384 samples. According to the beam-test vesults at CERN in 1992 and 1993 , an average SI/N ratio of 30 and a best spatial resolution of 3.5+-0.5/spl mu/m with an efficiency close to100% were obtained for the ONO-SMD.

articleTitle: Fabrication of organic polymer waveguides
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this paper, we present polymer waveguides fabricated by embossing with a micromachined silicon mould. The experimental results show that the embossed polymer waveguides provide a potential alternative for low cost mass production of optical interconnections.

articleTitle: Investigation of InGaAsP Transition layers for Aluminum-free InGaAs/GaAs/InGaP Strained- Quantum-Well Lasers
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Aluminum-free InGaAs/GaAs/InGaP strained quantum well laser with high characteristic temperature of 170 K is reported. The as-cleaved lasers with InGaAsP transition layers show internal quantum efficiency of 87 % and internal waveguide loss of 6.33 cm/sup -1/

articleTitle: 0.2 /spl mu/m AlGaAs/InGaAs pseudomorphic HEMT fabricated by optical lithography
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Al/sub 0.2/Ga/sub 0.8/As/ln/sub 0.25/Ga/sub 0.75/As pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistors (PHEMTs) with a 0.2-/spl mu/m gate length have been fabricated. Based on a shadow deposition technique, the sub-half-micron gate length technology using optical lithography has been developed. This process exhibits large cross-sectional area of the gate to reduce the gate resistance of devices. The gate resistance of 46 /spl omega//mm of gate width was obtained for a 5000 A thick Ti/Au gate. In addition, a PHEMT fabricated with this technique yielded cut-off frequency of f/sub T/ = 36 GHz and maximum oscillation frequency of f/sub max/ = 93 GHz.

articleTitle: The carrier transport in the GaSb/AiSb/lnAs/GaSb/AlSb/InAs resonant interband tunneling structures
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The negative differential resistance (NDR) characteristics of GaSb/AlSb/GaSb/AISb/lnAs double barrier structure were improved by incorporating an InAs blocking layer into the well region, i.e. GaSb/AlSb/InAs/GaSb/AlSb/InAs structure. The multiple NDR behaviors as well as high peak-to-valley ratios (PVRs) were observed with appropriate InAs well width. The three-band model was used to investigate the effect of the InAs well on the current-voltage characteristics of GaSb/AlSb/lnAs/GaSb/AISb/lnAs structures.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the gate lag phenomena in GaAs MESFET's
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A two-dimensional transient simulation of the gate lag phenomenon in GaAs MESFET's has been performed. Our results show that the charge exchanges in the population of the surface states at the ungated access region of FET's are responsible for this slow transient phenomenon. The measured "hole-trap-like" DLTS signal is directly related to the re-emission of the holes, trapped during the filling pulse. Devices with lower surface state densities are shown to have less gate lag effect.

articleTitle: Molecular beam epitaxy regrowth of pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistors using thin in layer
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We have demonstrated a molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) regrowth technique on GaAs Substrate using thin In-passivation layer. After the growth of buffer layers, the substrate temperature was lowered to deposit a thin In layer at about 50/spl deg/C, to ensure a uniform In coverage. These samples were then removed from the MBE system and left at atmosphere for weeks, before being reloaded back to MBE for the regrowth of a pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (PHEMT). Hall measurements indicated comparable results between the regrowth and reference samples. C -V depth profiling on the regrown PHEMT revealed no sign of residual charge-carriers at the interface. The regrown PHEMT with 1-um gate length has transconductance as high as 330 mS/mm and f/sub T/ of 23 GHz. These results indicate the In-regrowth may serve as a useful technique for obtaining complex circuits on the same chip.

articleTitle: GaAs-based high temperature digital circuits
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We report on GaAs-MESFET based digital logic circuits that operate from room temperature to over 300/spl deg/C. Circuit operation is achieved using a novel technique/technology that results in substantial improvements in device performance and reduction of the parasitic and leakage currents in gallium arsenide (GaAs) metal semiconductor field effect transistor (MESFET) devices and circuits at elevated temperatures up to 350/spl deg/C. This technique/technology also allows a wide range of control with respect to the MESFET's enhanced resistance to breakdown at elevated temperatures. The technique/technology has general applicability and works equally well with both enhancement and depletion n-channel MESFETs.

articleTitle: New metal structure by sidewall encapsulation method
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The microvoids or etch defects are occurred at the sidewall of metal line where is one of the weak points against stress induced migration (SM) and electromigration (EM). These defects result in metal line failure so that degrade reliability of metal line. Until now, sidewall hillock or sidewall defect has been reported, but the suppression method is not suggested. In this report, newly developed metal line structure by sidewall-encapsulation technique is proposed, which is to make an Al/sub 3/Ti and/or Al/sub 12/W intermetallic compound at the sidewall of metal line by deposition of Ti, TiN, or TiW on the patterned metal line. Therefore, this technique provides some advantages such as an application of Al-reflow process, the improvement of SM resistance and EM lifetime, and sidewall hillock suppression. Additionally, using AES depth profiles and SEM, the obtained results are analyzed to prove the mechanism of reliability improvement.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations of kink phenomena and the related backgating effect in GaAs MESFETs
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Two-dimensional simulations of GaAs MESFETs are made in which impact ionization of carriers and deep levels in the semi-insulating substrate are considered. It is shown that the kink or sub-breakdown is explained by impact ionization of holes and the following hole trapping (or hole accumulation) in the substrate rather than by direct gate breakdown. In addition, the kink-related backgating effect is reproduced by our simulation for the first time, and its mechanism is clarified.

articleTitle: Design of C+ -implantation conditions by trim calculation for ion beam defect engineering in Ge+ -preamorphized and BF/sub 2/+ -implanted silicon
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: TRIM cascade calculations were utilized to simulate the defect production and energy deposition in the ion implanted silicon. A guide line for carbon ion beam defect engineering implant is obtained to reduce the size of residual defects in the high energy Ge+ preamorphized and low energy BF/sub 2/+ implanted silicon.

articleTitle: The effect of hydrogenous species on the properties and reliability of the dielectrics and metals used in multilevel metallization
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The most important metallization problems in the electronics industry arise from the mass transport induced by either a chemical potential gradient (interdiffusion) or high current density (electromigration). There is ample evidence that hydrogen can provide substantial reduction of the mass transport caused by these two forces and also of the 1/f noise. Hydrogenous species are also found to play an important role in controlling electrical and mechanical properties of the insulators generally used on the chips. Such effects will play a critical role in changing our materials and their processing paths as well as their use. In this paper we bring focus to these effects by presenting and discussing the results of our investigations of the effect of hydrogen on (a) the interactions of copper with Ti, Mg, CoSi/sub 2/ and (b) the resistance and noise in gold metallization, (c) the electromigration in Al, and (d) the electrical and mechanical properties of the SiO/sub 2/ films.

articleTitle: The characteristics of ammonia-annealed polysilicon thin-film transistors with plasma hydrogenation
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The NH/sub 3/-annealing and the H/sub 2/-plasma hydrogenation techniques were jointly used to improve the characteristics of polysilicon thin-film transistors (TFT's). It was found that the TFT's after applying the above treatments achieved better subthreshold swings, threshold , voltages, field effect mobilities, off currents, and reliability. It is believed that the improvement was due to the gate oxynitride formation and the better H/sub 2-plasma response on the TFT with the gate oxynitride.
