publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A three order of magnitude enhancement of integrated photoluminescence (PL) intensity and a large red shift of 90 meV PL peak energy are observed in Al/sub 0.22/As grown on

articleTitle: Compositional disordering of AlGaAs/GaAs superlattices by low temperature grown GaAs
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The use of low-temperature (/spl tilde/ 200 /spl deg/C) grown GaAs by molecular beam epitaxy to induce compositional disordering of AlGaAs/GaAs superlattice has been studied. After furnace annealing between 700 /spl deg/C and 850 /spl deg/C for 30 minutes, obvious blue shift in the peak wavelength of the superlattice emission is observed by the 77K photoluminescence (PL), indicating that the emission has been changed from that of the GaAs quantum wells to that of the intermixed AlGaAs. The PL shift and the depth profile of Al concentration measured by secondary ion mass spectrometry indicate that the superlattice is nearly totally disordered after 850 /spl deg/C annealing.

articleTitle: Challenges for predictive process simulation in sub 0.1/spl mu/ silicon devices
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The promise of process simulation has always been that it could replace costly experiments in the development of new technology. The reality has been far less, primarily because of deficiencies in the physical models underlying such simulations. This situation is changing rapidly however, as better physically based models are developed. We may be finally reaching the time when TCAD tools can do much more than "model yesterday's technology tomorrow".

articleTitle: Ultra shallow n/sup+//p junctions formed by out-diffusion from TiSi/sub 2/ with an amorphous silicon buffer layer
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper presents a novel technology for ultra-shallow n/sup +/p junctions with low leakage current developed for the use of ULSI with scaled MOSFET's. The formation of shallow silicided junctions was investigated by implanting As into the TiSi/sub 2/ layer and the subsequent drive-in of the implanted arsenic into the Si substrate by a N/sub 2/ furnace. The TiSi/sub 2/ layer was formed by reaction of a deposited titanium with /spl alpha/ silicon. The junction quality is comparable to the conventional process (ITS). The major advantage of this process is more shallow junction depth than ITS's process. It is due to the depositied /spl alpha/-silicon film as a buffer layer that bulk-Si consumption during the silicidation process could be avoided.

articleTitle: Insb photo-mosfet fabricated by photo-enhanced chemical vapor deposition
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this paper, a new InSb infrared (IR) device is proposed and could be used as an unit cell of InSb monolithic IR focal plane array. Because the structure of the new InSb IR device is based on InSb metal-oxide-semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET), it is named as "InSb photo-MOSFET". The achieved quantum efficiency and specific detectivity is 0.53 and 4 x 10/sup 10/ cm x /spl radic/HZ/W respectively. This InSb photo-MOSFET can be used as an unit cell of InSb mono lithic IR array.

articleTitle: Interdisciplinary characterization of sandwiched SiGe thin layers grown by molecular beam epitaxy
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Si/sub 1-x/Ge/sub x/ layers sandwiched between Si were grown at low temperature of 450/spl deg/C by molecular beam epitaxy. A comprehensive characterization on these heterostructures by various techniques of x-ray diffraction, photoluminescence, Raman scattering, Fourier infrared spectroscopy, Rutherford backscattering spectrometry, ion channeling and secondary ion mass spectroscopy is presented.

articleTitle: Epitaxial growth of AlAs/sub x/Sb/sub 1-x/ by MOCVD
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The deposition of AlAs/sub x/Sb/sub 1-x/ films is studied systematically using an metalorganic chemical vapor deposition growth technique. It is found that the growth of AlAsSb films requires a low V/III ratio to enhance the incorporation of antimony into the solid. The composition of the alloy also depends strongly on the growth temperature. Experimental data shows that films grown at higher temperatures yield much higher AlSb contents in the AlAs/sub x/Sb/sub 1-x/ alloys. This is contrary to the results reported for GaAsSb films. In our study, we are able to grow metastable AlAs/sub x/Sb/spl 1-x/ epitaxial films throughout the entire range of the solid composition for temperatures above 550 /spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Trend for future silicon technology
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium

articleTitle: The effect of doping profile variations upon deep submicrometer MOSFET's
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The variations in current induced by variations in the (horizontal) doping profile between channel and drain or source can be described in terms of the variation in effective channel length, L/sub EFF/. Sensitivity becomes severe as L/sub EFF/ /spl rarr/0. On the other hand, for doping variations normal to the channel that affect threshold voltage and turn-off, sensitivity is particularly strong in the subthreshold region. The centroid of the vertical profile must be controlled to sub-Debye length accuracy to keep current variations below a few percent.

articleTitle: Characterization of deep submicron pattern and quantum dots using atomic force microscope(AFM)
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: AFM was empolyed as an inspection and metrology tool for the deep submicron pattern on photomask and Si wafer and the quantum dots on GaAs substrate. Good preformance is obtained.

articleTitle: High hole mobility transistor (HHMT) with dual Si/Ge/sub 0.4/Si/sub 0.6/Si wells structure grown by Si MBE
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this work, a novel dual-well structure GeSi-channel p-MESFET grown by silicon molecular-beam epitaxy has been proposed. Based on Hall measurements, a hole mobility of as high as 2680

articleTitle: Effects of scaling and radiation on BiCMOS switching
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: BiCMOS transient response including scaling, high current, and radiation effects has been studied. During the transient response minority carriers of the BJT are injected into the epitaxial region, widening the electrical base of the device and thus reducing current gain and the switching speed of the BiCMOS inverter. The BiCMOS gate delay decreases with increasing temperature and increases with decreasing power supply voltage. Radiation causes degradation of minority carrier life time and hence results in a decrease of the current gain of the BJT and an increasing BiCMOS switching delay.

articleTitle: A new measurement technique for capacitive coupling coefficients and 3-D capacitance characteristics in floating-gate devices
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A new technique is presented herein by which to measure accurately the capacitive coupling coefficient (/spl alpha/sub c/) between the control and floating gates in the ON-state of the device during the programming. The results obtained are compared with those found from other methods. It is also shown that a set of /spl alpha/-data obtained from test patterns with varying floating gate widths in the subthreshold region leads to the 3-D characterization of small geometry floating-gate devices down to subfemto Farads. These measured characteristics are discussed in light of the effects of the short channel length and of the narrow gate width.

articleTitle: Memory cell technology for high performance SRAMs
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A memory cell design and fabrication process for high performance SRAMs are described. Stacked Split Word-Line cell architecture achieves 7.16/spl mu/m/sup 2/ cell area with relaxed 0.4/spl mu/m design rule. Pull-down and access transistors of the memory cell are carefully and independently designed to enhance cell stability. High performance polysilicon thin film transistor is realized by channel polysilicon oxidation and oxygen assisted hydrogen passivation into channel polysilicon. Fabrication process steps are designed to reduce mechanical stress that causes large memory cell leakage and degrades data retention stability.

articleTitle: Planarizing dielectrics for VLSI technology
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this paper we describe the first reported blanket removal properties of various dielectric films. Based on material selectivity, We deposited thin PEOX, thick BPSG and a hard dielectric film with lower removal rate on top of a patterned wafer. Initial polishing removed the top hard dielectric level completely, exposing the BPSG, but the lower hard material remains less polished, BPSG polishes faster than hard dielectric film, resulting that the BPSG level was selectively polished. After the completion of the process with over etch, the height variation of 5mm scan range is less than 60 nm.

articleTitle: The electrical properties of rf sputtered tantalum oxide films
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Quasi-static and high frequency capacitance versus voltage (C-V) and current versus time (I-t) measurements of Al/Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/SiO/sub 2/Si (MTOS) capacitors are analyzed. Space charge build-up at the Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5//SiO/sub 2/ interface and the frequency response of these charges are explained. From the C-V results, it was found that the leakage current was not the sole contributor to the discrepancies observed in the quasi-static measurements, as suggested in the literature. The charge at the Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5//SiO/sub 2/ interface was used to explain the current transient. This interface charge density was calculated from the I-t curve and was found to be 3.17x10/sup -7/C cm /sup -2/

articleTitle: The electrical and optical properties of implanted amorphous silicon
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The n-type amorphous silicon hydrogen alloys are prepared by phosphorus ion implantation, followed by thermal annealing and hydrogen passivation. A critical dosage of 5x10/sup15/ is found, beyond which the doping effect become evident and the electrical properties of the film is comparable to the n/sup +/ a-Si:H deposited by glow discharge. From the IR spectra of the highly implanted samples, the SiH/sub x/ species become very small after hydrogen passivation. It is due to the fact that most of the voids are filled by extra P atoms during annealing, so very few hydrogen atoms can be driven into the film. In photoluminescence spectra, the high energy peak at 1.4 eV drops very fast and low energy shoulder at 1.25 eV becomes evident after implantation. It can be explained by Brodsky's quantum well model.

articleTitle: High effective channel mobility back junction SiGe pmos: theory of operation
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The theory of operation for the high effective channel mobility back junction SiGe PMOS is presented. The reduction of the vertical electric field and the improvement in hole confinement are explained physically. An analytical back junction bias dependent threshold voltage model is derived and verified by numerical simulation. Comparison to the back junction full Si device shows that the punch through between the channel and the substrate is effectively suppressed by the SiGe/Si hetero-junction.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional bi-periodic grating coupled one- and two-color quantum well infrared photodetectors
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Multiple quantum well infrared photodetectors (QWlPs) with two-dimensional bi-periodic grating couplers have been demonstrated. The two-dimensional grating has two different grating periods in the transverse and the longitudinal directions. For one-color QWIPs, the response linewidths of such QWIPs are found to be much wider than those of conventional grating coupled QWIPs. The bi periodic gratings have also been applied to two-color QWIPs to separately optimize the absorption at two wavelength bands. The Large difference in responsivities at the two wavelength bands for devices with single period gratings can be greatly reduced with the use of bi-periodic gratings.

articleTitle: Noise properties of ultrasmall resonant-tunneling diodes
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We report a theoretical study of the noise properties of an ultrasmall resonant-tunneling structure. An analytical expression is derived for the noise power spectrum with the equation-of-motion method. We study the noise behavior as a function of both the bias voltage and the barriers, and find that the correlation between elections induced by the Coulomb repulsion ran suppress the noise significantly, which should be observable in a noise measurement.

articleTitle: Monolithic tunable semiconductor lasers using photon recycling
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A novel monolithic tunable semiconductor laser is demonstrated. It consists of a laser diode integrated on top of a photodiode. The tunable range of this device depends on the optical coupling between the laser diode and the photodiode. Through photon recycling, the threshold pump power and the threshold current of the device were reduced by 21.1% and 5.1%, respectively. According to our model, the 5.1% reduction of the threshold current corresponded to a calculated 3.3 nm wavelength shift.

articleTitle: High quality low-temperature GaAs film grown by conventional metalorganic chemical vapor deposition
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper offers a convenient method to grow good quality of GaAs films at low-temperature ( LT ) , 425 /spl deg/C, by using conventional metalorganic chemical vapor deposition ( MOCVD ) growth technique and taking tertiarybutylarsine ( TBAs ) along with triethylgallium ( TEGa ) as the epitaxial sources . By taking the results from 77 K PL and double crystal X-ray, the film grown at 425 /spl deg/C has shown a full width at half maximum ( FWHM ) 8.2 meV and 14 arcsec . These results indicate that high quality of GaAs films can be obtained by using conventional MOCVD technique without setting any extra and external equipments.

articleTitle: A novel LOCOS SPI (self-aligned-pocket-implantation) technology for a half micron NMOSFET
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A novel LOCOS SPI technology has been developed. This, technology is characterized by a localized "pocket" implantation using LOCOS for device isolation and gate electrode as self-aligned masks. We have made a half micron NMOSFET which suppressed the short channel effect and featured a subthreshold swing of 93mV/dec. Parasitic drain junction capacitance of LOCOS SPI NMOSFET has been decreased by 10% compared to conventional LDD device, which we expect could reduce a delay time significantly and thus enable the high speed operation.

articleTitle: Vibrational local modes of a-Si:(h,c) alloys
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The cluster-Bethe-lattice method is used to study the vibrational properties of the a Si:(H,C) alloys. The isolated Si/sub 4/C, H-Si-C, Si-CH/sub 3/, and Si/sub 3/C- (Carbon with a dangling bond) groups in a-Si:(H,C) alloys are under investigation. The vibrational local density of states for these local bonding structures are calculated. The Si-C bond-stretching mode of the isolated Si/sub 4/C group is at 780 cm/sup -1/. For the H-Si-C matrix, we have the Si-H bond-stretching and bond-bending modes respectively at 2080 and 630 cm/sup -1/, and the Si-C bond-stretching at 780 cm/sup -1/. The local modes for the Si-CH/sub 3/ group are the C-H bond-stretching modes at 2950 and 2878 cm/sup -1/, and the deformation modes at 1240 and 1180 cm/sup -1/. All these results are generally agreed with the experimental data. The Si-C stretching mode for C with a dangling bond shifts to a lower value of 748 cm/sup -1/.

articleTitle: Base transit time of submicron bipolar transistors including nonuniform base doping profile and high current effects
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: An analytical /spl tau//sub B/ model of submicron bipolar transistors valid for arbitrary levels of injection and Gaussian base doping profile is presented in this paper. For the devices considered, our calculations show that the conventional model (considers uniform base doping profile and no base pushout) overestimates /spl tau//sub B/ by a factor of about 2.5 at low injection and underestimates /spl tau//sub B/ by a factor of about 1.5 at high injection. Besides, /spl tau//sub EC/ calculated from present model compares favorably with experimental data measured from a 0. 12 /spl mu/m base width BJT.

articleTitle: High dielectric constant Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ thin films prepared by rf magnetron sputtering for dynamic random access memory applications
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: High dielectric constant Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ capacitors intended for dynamic random access memory applications are investigated. Capacitors with a Au/Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5//Pt/Ti structure on silicon wafer are fabricated. The Ta/sub 2/O/sub 5/ thin film is deposited by rf magnetron sputtering. The thin film material property is examined by X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy. The electrical performances related to dynamic random access memory applications are examined. The leakage current is on the order of 10/sup -7/ A/cm/sup 2/ at an applied field of 1 MV/cm for a film thickness 800 A. The leakage current mechanism is attributed to Schottky emission at low field below 0.3 MV/cm and Fowler-Nordheim tunneling at high field above 0.5 MV/cm

articleTitle: Field effect controlled transferred electron device with two negative resistance regions
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: For advancing the developemt of mono lithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs), field effect controlled fransferred electron de vice (FECTED) combined with the design of coplanar waveguide have been proposed. In order to match the external circuits and mini mize the energy loss, we designed a coplanar wave guide with 50 /spl Omega/ characteristic i-mpedance. The device is design to have ohmic cathode contact, Schottky gate and anode contact over the epilayer(s) of a semi-insulating GaAs wafer. The results show that the device with single epilayer will have negative differential resistance (NDR) in the I-V characteristic curve. It is observed that the I-V curve will have two NDR region if the active layer contained two n-type GaAs epilayers.

articleTitle: A novel In/sub 0.49/Ga/sub 0.51/P/GaAs MSM photodetector
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A novel high-performance GaAs metal semiconductor-metal photodetector (MSM-PD), with an undoped In/sub 0.49/Ga/sub 0.51/P capping layer, is reported in this paper. The main features of this device include: low dark current of less than 8 nA, low capacitance of 140 fF at 10 V with device area of 75x75 /spl mu/m/sup 2/; short rise time of 25 ps at 8 V; and a high responsivity of 0.43 A/W with the wide linear responsivity region (ranged from 1 to 100 /spl mu/W at 10 V) for /spl lambda/ = 0.83 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: A new buffered p+ poly-gate for suppression of boron penetration effect
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This work reports the use of amorphous/polysilicon gate electrode in BF/sub 2//sup +/ -implanted poly-gated P-MOSFET's to suppress the boron penetration effect. Superior short-channel behavior and less boron penetration effect are obtained for the new gate structure as indicated by the experimental results. The textures of these two layers are different which may be the cause of retardation of boron penetration. Results show that the structure is a promising gate electrode for future dual-poly gate CMOS technology development.

articleTitle: Base current noise degradation of polysilicon emitter npn bjt during constant-current stress
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The varity of base current noise of nonwalled and walled types polysilicon emitter npn B JT were measured, under the same constant current stress. We find the degradation of noise of walled type is larger than that of nonwalled type when the stress was oprated at very high current condition.

articleTitle: Non-stationary effect in ultra small mos devices
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The non-stationary effects in ultra small MOS devices with the gate length of 0.1/spl mu/m or sub-0.1/spl mu/m have been evaluated. As for the non stationary effect in the carrier transport, the velocity overshoot effect is mainly investigated using Monte Carlo simulator. The non stationary effect in the impact ionization effect is also investigated based on the experimental results. It is shown that the impact ionization factor in the low drain voltage region decreases due to the decreased electron energy as the temperature is lowered.

articleTitle: Electroreflectance measurements of triple quantum well structures
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Electroreflectance measurements have been carried out to clarify the resonant coupling between the states in an asymmetric triple quantum well structure. The triple quantum well structure consists of three kinds of quantum wells with different widths, and their widths are designed so that the ground states of the three wells in the conduction band would be at resonance under a certain electric field. The electroreflectance spectra reveal six types of optical transitions which indicate a clear resonant coupling between the wells at about 17 kV/cm. The transition energies are found to agree well with the calculated results.

articleTitle: 1.5 /spl mu/m GRIN-SCH strained multi-quantum-well ridge-waveguide lasers for high-speed optical communication
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Device characteristics of 1.5 /spl mu/m strained multi quantum-well (MQW) ridge-waveguide (RWG) laser diodes are presented. A highest 3-dB modulation bandwidth of 5 GHz was achieved, demonstrating potential applications of these lasers for high speed and long distance optical communication.

articleTitle: High pressure field oxidation for advanced poly-buffered locos isolation process
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: This paper presents the results of high Pressure Oxidation applied to the Poly-Buffered LOCOS isolation process for 1.0/spl mu/m pitch design rules. This research demonstrates that high pressure field oxidation can reduce bird's beak encroachment at temperatures about 1000/spl deg/C relative to atmospheric field oxidation, and it can also appreciably improve the field oxide thinning in sub-half-micron spaces as low as 0.35/spl mu/m at temperatures above 1000/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: An analytical model and experimental results of a highly integrateable magnetic field sensor
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: An analytical model, supported by both experimental and simulation results, of a split-drain CMOS transistor for use as a magnetic sensor is described. We show that the sensitivity is a function of the roll-off of the Hall potential and not due to channel inversion charge redistribution. In addition, the sensitivity is not a function of geometry, linear to magnetic field strength, and affected by the gap between the 2 drains.

articleTitle: Thermal stability of Cu/CoSi/sub 2/ contacted p/sup +/n shallow junction with and without TiN/sub x/ diffusion barrier
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The thermal stability of Cu/CoSi/sub 2/ contacted p/sup +/ n shallow junction diodes with and without TiN diffusion barrier was investigated with respect to metallurgical reaction and electrical characteristics. Without the diffusion barrier, the Cu(2000A)/CoSi/sub 2/(700A)/p/sup +/n diodes (with a junction depth of 0.2 /spl mu/m measured from the silicide surface) were able to sustain a 30s rapid thermal annealing (RTA) in N/sub 2/ ambient up to 450/spl deg/C without losing the integrity of the devices' characteristics. The Cu/sub 3/Si phase was observed at the CoSi/sub 2//Si interface after 500/spl deg/C annealing; the phase penetrated through the CoSi/sub 2/ layer causing a catastrophic change in layer structure after 700/spl deg/C annealing. With the addition of a 1200A thickness of TiN/sub x/ diffusion barrier between Cu and CoSi/sub 2/, the junction diodes were able to sustain the RTA treatment up to 550/spl deg/C without degrading the electrical characteristics, and the Cu/sub 3/Si phase can be observed only after annealing at temperatures above 600/spl deg/C. The failure of the devices resulted from the Cu penetration through the TiN/sub x/ and CoSi/sub 2/ layers leading to junction degradation either by acting as the deep trapping levels or by reacting with Si to form the Cu/sub 3/Si compound.

articleTitle: A general purpose hydrodynamic solver for the simulation of semiconductor devices
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We have developed a general purpose 2-D HD solver which is capable of solving different HD models on virtually the same computer code. The code is written so that it dose not depend on a specific form of the model/parameters which is only introduced at the final stage.

articleTitle: A closed-form physical model for vlsi bipolar devices considering energy transport
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: iThis paper reports a closed-form analytical model for VLSI BJT devices considering energy transport for the first time. As verified by the PISCES data, the closed-form analytical model shows a good accuracy in predicting the collector current.

articleTitle: Design of multiple-quantum-well electroabsorption surface-normal modulators using asymmetric fabry-perot structures
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We presented a systematic approach for optimizing the performance of a multiple-quantum-well eleectroabsorption surface-normal modulator using asymmetric Fabry-Perot structures.The primary requirements of these modulators are low drive voltage,high contrast ratio(CR), low insertion loss,and high speed.For specified high CR(> 20dB) requirement, maximizing /spl Delta//spl alpha//sub max///spl Delta/ of the material structure,where /spl Delta//spl alpha//sub max/ is the maximum absorption change and /spl Delta/F is the corresponding applied electric field, or adopting R/sub T/ /spl tilde/ 60% of asymmetric Fabry-Perot etalon can obtain low-drive voltage modulator. There are trade-off between the requirements of low-drive-voltage and high frequency-response.The criterion of the optimization is to maximum /spl Delta//spl alpha//spl Delta/F/sup 2/. Our theoretical model shows that wider wells give large /spl Delta//spl alpha//sub max///spl Delta/F/sup 2/ for ASFP modulators.

articleTitle: Active hollow four quadrant orientation detector array for applications to pattern recognition
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The active hollow FOur QUadrant Orientation Detector (active hollow FOQUOD) two dimensional 8 ' 8 array using amorphous silicon material deposited on a silicon substrate has been fabricated successfully. This array can extract the contrast edges and the edge orientations of the test patterns and the pixel yield is close to 100 percent. Since the measured patterns are consistent with the expected results, part of the traditional data processing steps using software may be replaced by this hardware sensor array, a simpler algorithm than ever had for pattern recognition can then be developed.

articleTitle: Effects of dry etching damage removal on Si selective epitaxial growth
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: After etching treatment (AET) performed in after treatment chamber (ATC) of a reactive ion etching (RIE) system was reported to be efficient in removing the residual layer and defects caused by RIE as well as producing a clean surface of oxide patterned windows for selective epitaxial growth (SEG). And, an interesting phenomenon that the AET time of full-patterned and half-patterned wafers was different with all other parameters fixed was observed.

articleTitle: A GaAs double negative differential resistance device with a p+ AlGaAs base
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a three-terminal i GaAs/p/sup +/ -AlGaAs/i-GaAs structure which exists two voltage-controllable and distinct N-shape negative differential resistance (NDR) regions at room temperature. Voltage extents in each NDR region are as large as 10 volts. Corresponding peak to valley current ratios (PVRs) for the first and second NDR regions are 43 and 7 at V/sub BE/=5V, respectively. By inserting the p/sup +/ -AlGaAs layer between undoped GaAs layers, two dimensional hole gas (DHG) may be formed. A tentative model responsible for two NDR regions based on the bipolar unipolar transition effect with the aid of tunneling effect is thus presented.

articleTitle: Deep center defects in AlGaAs/GaAs grin-sch sqw lasers fabricated by MBE and MOCVD
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The deep center traps of AlGaAs/GaAs GRIN-SCH SQW lasers fabricated by MBE and MOCVD have been studied using DLTS (Deep Level Transient Spectroscopy) technique.The DLTS spectra show that deep (electron and hole) traps, having larger capture cross sections and concentrations, are observed in n-AlGaAs layers of lasers in addition to the well-known DX center. For the MBE lasers, deep hole trap H1 may spatially localize in the interfacial regions of discontinous variation A1 mole fraction of n AlGaAs layers with X/sub AI/=0.20 /spl rarr/0.43 and X/sub AI=0.43/, and deep electron trap E3 may spatially localize in interfacial regions of discontinous variation Al mole fraction of n AlGaAs layer with X/sub AI=0.43/.For the MOCVD lasers,deep electron trap E3 may spatially localize in n-AlGaAs layers with X/sub Al/=0.18 /spl rarr/0.30 and X/sub AI/=0.30 and DX center may spatially localize in the interfacial regions of discontinous variation Al mole fraction of n-AlGaAs layers with X/sub AI/=0.18 /spl rarr/0.30 mid X/sub AI/=0.30.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of intrinsic capacitances for a fully depleted SOI MOSFET
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Based on the intrinsic capacitances model of bulk MOSFETs, a counterpart equivalent circuit model for the fully depleted SOI MOSFET is developed by emphasizing the structural uniqueness of the device. Under quasistatic operation condition, the intrinsic capacitances valid for all regions of operation, including weak and moderate inversion, are derived and computed by using the theories proposed recently [1]. The numerical simulations for both the depleted and accumulated back surfaces are presented, and the results are compared with those from the experiment and strong inversion theory.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional calculation of transient terminal currents in amorphous silicon thin-film transistors
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We report two-dimensional transient behavior at both switch-on and switch-off of amorphous silicon thin-film transistors. The trap filling time determines the switch-on time and the trap emptying time determines the switch-off time as compared to the transit time. The occupation functions for switch-on and switch-off are both non-Fermi distribution, but they are not time reversal. There exists a terminal current peak around the transit time at switch-off. This behavior is different from the behavior of transit terminal currents at switch-on.

articleTitle: Low capacitance, front-illuminated planar InGaAs PIN photodiode on semi-insulating InP substrate
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We have developed a simple, high yield process to fabricate low-capacitance, front-illuminated InGaAs/InP pin photodiodes on semi-insulating InP substrate. The fabricated devices have a very low capacitance smaller than 0.15pF with a 30 /spl mu/m junction diameter. The measured responsivity using fiber coupling is as high as 0.78 A/W at a wavelength of 1.55/spl mu/m. The low-capacitance photodiode results in a 3-dB bandwidth of 14.8 GHz which appears to be limited by carrier transit time rather than the RC time constant. These characteristics are expected to meet the stringent requirements in high speed and high sensitivity lightwave systems.

articleTitle: Ion-implanted GaAs MESFET's with W/WN/sub x/ bi-layer gate designs
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Characteristics of WNx films, deposited by a RF sputter, were evaluated through high temperature heat treatment. WNx films present themselves as a thermally stable material, which is suitable for gate material used in ion-implanted metal-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MESFET's). A bi-layer WNx/W film structutre was proposed for the purpose of reducing sheet resistivity, while remaining the high thermal stability properties. DC and RF performance of Ion-implanted GaAs MESFET's fabricated by both WNx and WNx/W gates were also characterized.

articleTitle: Identification of tunneling peaks in the GaAs/AlAs/GaAs resonant tunneling diode by magnetic fields
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The two tunneling mechanisms of the X band resonant tunneling and X band electrons tunneling through the r band confined states can be verified by applying the magnetic field to these structures. For X band electrons tunneling through the X band profile, the peak current and peak voltage remain the same whether the magnetic field is transverse or parallel to the current flow direction. However, for X band electrons tunneling through r band confined state, the peak current and peak voltage vary significantly with the transverse magnetic field but change much less with the parallel magnetic field.

articleTitle: Two x-band monolithic voltage controlled oscillators
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this paper, two types of MMIC voltage controlled oscillators have been successfully demonstrated. The first chip with single tuning diode shows the excellent tuning linearity. The second chip with two tuning diodes can improve the tuning bandwidth. The measured results of VCO with single diode shows the tuning bandwidth of 800 MHz centered at 9.2 GHz with the output power of 12 dBm. The second VCO with dual tuning diodes shows the tuning bandwidth of 2 GHz centered at 9.4 GHz The VCOs are fabricated with Hughes 0.5 micron ion implant MESFET foundry process[1].

articleTitle: Photoluminescence mechanisms in porous silicon
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: It is found that the lateral etching rate increases with increasing intensities of photo-irradiation during electrochemical etching of porous silicon until its bandgap becomes larger than the photon energies. The corresponding photoluminescence peak energies blueshift then saturate. These suggest that the photoluminescence spectra of the as fabricated samples are controlled by the quantum size effect. On the other hand, It is shown that the transitions between the oxide levels produce the photoluminescence with the peak position at about 1.7 eV, because the photoluminescence peak energies of the as fabricated samples ranging from 1.45 to 1.92 eV shift toward 1.7 eV after the samples axe oxidized in air for a period of time. Both the quantum size effect and the oxide related transitions should be attributed to the photoluminescence mechanisms.

articleTitle: Analysis of interface state induced performance variation in LDD MOSFET's
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We have performed a two-dimensional analysis to study the interface trap effects on the drain current degradation in submicron MOSFET's. A hot electron stress induced interface trap generation model has been developed. Mobility degradation and reduction of conduction charge due to interface traps are considered. A 0.6 /spl mu/m LDD MOSFET was stressed at V/sub ds/=7V and V/sub gs/=3V for 10/sup 4/ seconds. The drain current degradation was characterized in both normal mode and reverse mode to compare the simulation. Our study shows that a significant drain current reduction appears in the linear region whil e the current reduction is only a few percentage points in the saturation region in normal mode. In reverse mode, the drain current degradation is significant in the entire region of operation.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of LPE-grown, erbium-doped InGaAs PIN photodiodes
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We demonstrate the fabrication and characteristics of a new InGaAs PIN photodiode employing Erbium source into the InGaAs growth solution for donor-gettering by liquid-phase epitaxy. The presence of Er provides effective gettering of donor impurities in the growth solution, which results in a decrease in electron concentration and strong suppression on donor-related luminescence transition. By using Er-doped InGaAs as the absorption layer in the PIN structure, the planar-type, front-illuminated PIN photododiodes at zero bias exhibited good quantum efficiencies of 83% at 1.6 /spl mu/m wavelength with antireflection coating. Devices on submount with 100 /spl mu/m diameter active area showed low capacitances of 0.65 pF, and the 3-dB bandwidth large than 3.8 GHz at -5V bias were measured. Morover, a clear, error-free, and symmetrical eye pattern was obtained for a length of 2/sup 31/ -1 pseudorandom non-retum-to-zero (NRZ) signal up to 2.5 Gb/s. These characteristics of the devices will meet the performance requirements of the long wavelength optical communication.

articleTitle: In/sub 0.29/Al/sub 0.71/As/In/sub 0.3/Ga/sub 0.7/As heterostructure field-effect transistors fabricated on GaAs substrates
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The unstrained or the so-called metamorphic In/sub 0.29/Al/sub 0.71/As/In/sub 0.3/Ga/sub 0.7/As heterostructure FETs (HFETs), including HEMTs and DCFETs, have been fabricated on GaAs substrates by using a compositionally step-graded buffer design. A peak extrinsic DC transconductance (gm) of 230 mS/mm and saturation current density of 385 mA/mm were measured from a HEMTs device with 0.6 /spl mu/m-long gate length. This device also shows a current-gain cut-off frequence (f/sub T/)of 23 GHz and a maximum available, gain cut-off frequency (f/sub max/) of 73 GHz. Based on the DCFETs, a g/sub m/ of 220 mS/mm and a full channel current of 400 mA/mm were achieved for a 1/spl mu/m-long gate device. Also, the RF performance of f/sub T/=22 GHz and f/sub max/=51 GHz have been obtained.

articleTitle: Thin bonded wafer SOI CMOS technology for low voltage high performance applications
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) is becoming more attractive for enhancing performance as MOSFET physical dimensions are scaled down. In this work, a 0.5 micron process using bonded SOI material is compared to bulk CMOS. The comparisons include electrical parameters, delay time, and speed power product.

articleTitle: Improvement in radiation hardness of n-MOSFET's with gate oxides prepared by multiple N/sub 2/O annealings
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Higher field-effect channel mobility and improved radiation hardness of n-MOSFET with gate oxide prepared by multiple rapid thermal N/sub 2/O annealings are reported. The samples with fresh gate oidde and conventional single N/sub 2/O annealed gate oxide with comparable annealing time are also compared.

articleTitle: Improvement of radiation hardness of MOS device by use of amorphous Si
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A novel technique is proposed and demonstrated to improve the radiation hardness of MOS capacitors. This approach can be stated briefly that the poly-Si gate electrode of MOS device is formed by use of amorphous-Si film. Experimental results show that the improvement of radiation hardness by this technique is due to the decrease of SiO/sub 2/-Si interfacial stress. The hydrogert concentration, which may be increased by this technique, also plays an important role on the radiation hardness of MOS capacitor. As this technique needs little change in the device fabrication process, it should be useful in practice.

articleTitle: A self-consistent approach to substrate current simulation in submicron MOSFETs
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: We report a self-consistent approach for substrate current simulation by incorporating an energy-dependent impact ionization (II) model in PISCES-2ET. Simulation results are presented for submicron conventional and LDD MOSFETs with comparison to experimental data.

articleTitle: Gas source MBE growth of InP under In-rich conditions
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this study, the epitaxial growth of InP was pushed to In-rich conditions. It was found that the InP growth rate was limited by the PH/sub 3/ flow rate and the excess In atoms would accumulate on the growing surface and thus roughen the surface morphology. Furthermore, the low 8K and 300K PL intensities of the InP epilayers grown under In-rich conditions may be due to the defects generated by the In droplets. However, by removing the In droplets on the surface or inserting a periodic interruption stage in the In-rich conditions, the 300K and 8K PL intensity was 40 and 3 times larger than that grown under P/sub 2/-stabilized conditions, respectively. This improvement may result from the higher migration ability of In atoms under In-rich conditions.

articleTitle: An X-band high power amplifier
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A two stage X-Band with 20 % efficient power amplifier is fabricated with 0.5 micron ion implant MESFET foundry process is presented. The amplifier shows 1 watt output power and 9 dB associated gain across the frequency band. The amplifier is monolithic circuit without any off-chip combining or tuning.

articleTitle: The performance and reliability of self-induced lightly-doped-drain polysilicon thin film transistors
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A novel polycrystalline silicon thin film transistor (poly-Si TFT) with high ON/OFF current ratio independent of gate bias is developed. We call this device self-induced lightly-doped-drain (SI-LDD) poly-Si TFT. Both gate oxide and the passivation layer were grown by liquid-phase deposition (LPD) method. This paper describes the electrical characteristics for the SI-LDD poly-Si TFT with thin active layer. The effects of electrical stress on characteristics are also described.

articleTitle: Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/ formation by wet oxidation of AlAs for GaAs MOS device
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Thermal oxidation of AlAs/GaAs was performed in N/sub 2/ bubbled H/sub 2/O vapor(95/spl deg/C) at 370 /spl deg/C, 400/spl deg/C, and 430/spl deg/C each for 3 hours. AlAs/GaAs structure was selectively converted to Al/sub 2/O/sub 3//GaAs structure at the oxidation temperature of 400/spl deg/C. From the high frecquency (100kHz) C-V charatersitics, fixed oxide charge density was estimated about 1x 10/sup 11//cm/sup 2/.

articleTitle: MBE grown GaAS-InGaAs quantum-well resonant tunneling switching device
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium

articleTitle: Visible photoluminescence wiht multiple peaks from the porous boron 5/spl delta/-doped Si superlattice
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In this work, we report the first study of the porous boron /delta/-doped Si superlattice. Visible photoluminescence (PL) with multiple peaks from the porous boron 6/spl delta/-doped Si superlattice was observed at room temperature. The multiple peaks of PL spectrum from the porous superlattice can be explained on the basis of interference from the periodic structure. The high-resolution double crystal x-ray diffraction (HRXRD) and scanning electron microscope (SEM) were used to investigate the dopant distribution and structure of these superlattices. In addition, theoretical transmittance of the porous superlattice with alternative refraction index was calculated to confirm the interference effect of the PL spectrum.

articleTitle: Characteristics of amorphous tungsten nitride diffusion barrier for metal-organic chemical vapor deposited Cu metallization
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Copper thin films are deposited on amorphous tungsten nitride diffusion barrier by metal organic chemical vapor deposition method. The resistivity of Cu film is considerably higher than those of Cu films deposited on SiO/sub 2/, borophospho-silica glass, and Si due to substrate driven reaction. RBS, XTEM and XRD measurements clearly show that 100-800 A amorphous W/sub 67/N/sub 33/ layer successfully executes the role of diffusion barrier for Cu during the annealing process at 800 /spl degC for 30 min.

articleTitle: Impact of SiGe heterostructures on silicon devices
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: In the past several attempts were made to combine the advantages of heterostructures with the dynamic development of silicon based microelectronics. Recently, the epitaxial growth of SiGe/Si heterostructures has been improved to a level that device demonstrations were possible. The most prominent example of these demonstrators is given by the 100 GHz heterobipolar transistor (HBT) which is surpassing even very sophisticated all silicon devices in several characteristics. This report deals with growth and electronic effects of SiGe/Si structures, with the device concepts based on these heterostructures, with the current status of device realizations, and gives an outlook for future directions.

articleTitle: AlGaAs/GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors with shifted junction
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The experimental and simulation results of AIGaAs/GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) with and without emitter-base (EB) junction shift to emitter are presented. Current gains are found to increase for 30 A while decrease dramatically for 100 A doping junction shift to emitter in abrupt HBTs. The offset voltage, turn-on voltage, and EB capacitance are also studied. From the simulation analysis, it is found that the stability of graded HBT is better than that of abrupt HBT as junction shift to emitter.

articleTitle: MBE growth of multilayer heterostructures with applications to optoelectronic and electronic devices
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: One of the most exciting and useful developments in modern semiconductor electronics is the capability of engineering band structure, quantum phenomena, optical properties, and other useful effects by the growth of multilayer heterostructures. With the advent of advanced semiconductor growth techniques such as molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and organometallic chemical vapor deposition (OMCVD), much of modern compound semiconductor device development now involves quite complex and precise multi heterojunction structures. The availability of high-quality multilayer heterostructures has led to new effects having widespread applications such as two-dimensional transport effects, quantum wells, modulation doping, delta doping, carrier and photon confinement, etc. Recently, distributed Bragg reflectors (DBR) have been added to this collection of capabilities. As a result, the future for device invention and development is extremely fertile, combining electronic and photonic effects in new ways for novel applications. Clearly, future computer and communication systems will increasingly depend on high-speed electronic, photonic, and microwave/millimeter wave devices based on these capabilities. In this talk we discuss some of these properties of multilayer heterostructures, with applications to electronic and photonic devices, particularly those employing resonant cavity structures, quantum wells, superlattices, and other unique features of advanced crystal growth techniques.

articleTitle: The effects of crystallinity and thickness of silicide layer and substrate orientation on the oxidation of NiSi/sub 2/ on silicon
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium

articleTitle: A comparative study of positive and negative bias temperature instabilities in MOSFETs
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium

articleTitle: Growth and investigation of quaternary III-III-III-V InGaAlAs alloy layers on InP by molecular beam epitaxy
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: A variety of III-V quaternary ln/sub 1-x-y/Ga/sub x/Al/sub y/As films, for use of 0.8-1.6 /spl mu/m emission optoelectronic devices, have been grown on InP by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE). A comprehensive characterization was performed using double crystal X-ray diffraction (DCXRD), Raman scattering, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, photoluminescence (PL), on these heterostructures with different compositions and growth conditions. The lattice matched and mismatched structures are studied. Our analyses show that the interface mismatch exerts an important influence on the optical properties of these heterostructures, and conversely that Raman, PL and FTIR which are powerful nondestructive tools, can be used to probe the interface mismatch.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

publicationTitle: International Electron Devices and Materials Symposium
abstract: Conference proceedings front matter may contain various advertisements, welcome messages, committee or program information, and other miscellaneous conference information. This may in some cases also include the cover art, table of contents, copyright statements, title-page or half title-pages, blank pages, venue maps or other general information relating to the conference that was part of the original conference proceedings.
